issues: Most samples share a smooth pale finish; the rubber ring looks especially glossy and plastic.
Painted metal, bare metal, and concrete have very similar visible responses.
The glass/light panel appears opaque and has no evident luminous response.
Concrete lacks visible grain or pores; broad surfaces show little material-specific variation.
The display base is cropped at both sides, though all samples and labels remain readable.
Shared sample and floor colors slightly weaken separation; overlaps, shading, and perspective still communicate depth.
Broad soft lighting produces restrained contrast, limiting differentiation across the large faces.
Contact shadows are visible and generally anchor the objects; the ring has a particularly clear contact point.
The clean display and simple silhouettes support stylization, but the uniform finish reads more like a material placeholder study than resolved industrial ACG materials.

bounded_actions.recommendation: Test subtle, material-local roughness variation on painted metal and concrete; avoid uniform noise across every sample.
Test a 10–20 degree more oblique key-light direction to reveal surface and face differences.
Widen framing by approximately 5–10% if the full display base should be visible.

separate_material_plan_review: Differentiate bare metal, painted metal, concrete, and rubber through their base material responses and appropriate surface detail.
Decide whether glass/light represents transmissive glass, an emissive fixture, or both; its current opaque appearance requires a material review, not merely roughness variation.
scope: Visual inspection of the supplied image only; no modification or approval.
